verdict.rationale: The only evidence of an open license is a community comment noting that Elastic now offers AGPL alongside the Elastic License, which implies the source can be read and self-hosted under an OSI-approved license. Older community comments describe the SSPL switch and a 'formerly-OSS core', but these predate the AGPL option rather than contradicting it. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license terms, a link to the core Elasticsearch source repository, and clarity on which features are AGPL versus proprietary-licensed.
